note: Hebrew gibbor chayil can mean a warrior or a man of wealth and standing; with no military context here it most likely describes Kish as a prominent, well-to-do man.

kjv: on whom is all the desire of Israel?
mine: for whom is all that is desirable in Israel?
note: Hebrew ul-mi kol-chemdat yisra'el, "to whom (belongs) all the desirable things of Israel"; the KJV makes Saul the object of Israel's longing, whereas the phrase more naturally refers to the wealth and honour of the nation passing to Saul's house.
Hebrew shoq is the leg or thigh (the priestly portion of Lev 7:32), not the shoulder (zeroa').
